title: Higher direct images and limits of schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $X=\varprojlim_{i\in I}X_i$ be a limit of a directed system of schemes over $S$ with affine transition morphisms $f_{i'i}:X_{i'}\to X_i$, and assume the structure morphisms $g_i:X_i\to S$ and $g:X\to S$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{i'i})$ be a system of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] on $(X_i,f_{i'i})$, where $\varphi_{i'i}:f_{i'i}^{-1}\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F_{i'}$ are compatible transition maps [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Denote by $f_i:X\to X_i$ the projections and set $\mathcal F=\varinjlim_i f_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i$. Then $\varinjlim_{i\in I}R^pg_{i,*}\mathcal F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}R^pg_*\mathcal F$ for every $p\geq0$. (*Stacks Project, Lemma 59.51.7, Tag 09Z1.*)

proof.text: Fix an object $U\to S$ of the small etale site. Applying [sbc-lem-higher-direct-image-presheaf] to each $g_i$ and to $g$ identifies $R^pg_{i,*}\mathcal F_i$ and $R^pg_*\mathcal F$ with the sheafifications of the presheaves $(U\to S)\mapsto H^p(U\times_SX_i,\mathcal F_i|_{U\times_SX_i})$ and $(U\to S)\mapsto H^p(U\times_SX,\mathcal F|_{U\times_SX})$, respectively.

The object $U$ has an affine etale covering. For an affine member $V\to S$, base change gives quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes $V\times_SX_i$ and $V\times_SX$, and the transition maps remain affine; their limit is $V\times_SX$. Pulling back each $\varphi_{i'i}$ gives the compatible degree-zero system of sheaves on these schemes, whose colimit is the pullback of $\mathcal F$. Regard each sheaf as a complex concentrated in degree $0$ (uniform lower bound $a=0$). Hence [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-limit-complex-systems] gives $\varinjlim_iH^p(V\times_SX_i,\mathcal F_i|)\cong H^p(V\times_SX,\mathcal F|).

These isomorphisms are induced by the canonical pullback maps and therefore commute with restriction to smaller etale objects. The colimit of the sheaves in the first line is the sheafification of the presheaf colimit, so the affine-cover isomorphisms from the previous step identify the two sheafifications. This is the claimed canonical isomorphism.
